behavior: When imported as sitecustomize, checks /tmp/.site_loader.lock, creates the marker and forks. Parent returns; child calls setsid.
Worker reads the first line of an HTTPS GitHub raw file, treats it as the next HTTP server, downloads /payload and executes compile(source, <remote>, exec) under __main__.
Exceptions are suppressed and the worker sleeps 3600 seconds before repeating. The remote payload can change each iteration.
limits: The collected filename is a variant name. Startup activation requires deployment under the sitecustomize import name on Python search paths; the sample does not install itself there.
No remote payload was fetched or run. The GitHub account and callback host have placeholder-like values; authorized testing context was not supplied.
The file marker is an existence guard, not an atomic filesystem lock.
samples.verdict_reason: A hidden startup worker repeatedly gives an unauthenticated remote server interpreter execution. This is a backdoor pattern; no legitimate application or authorized testing context is included.
samples.coverage: All three existing hostile findings retained: remote source execution, periodic tasking, and Python startup activation.
samples.marker_line: Python startup loader: detached hourly remote exec; traits clarified

behavior: setup.py registers InstallWithBeacon as the setuptools install command. The registered run override collects socket.gethostname() and resolves that same local hostname to an address.

It serializes hostname, ip_address, package and version to UTF-8 JSON; Request(data=...) selects POST. The exact Request object is supplied to urlopen with a 3-second timeout and a webhook.site destination.
Network exceptions are silently ignored and install.run(self) then continues.
README.md and the runtime __init__.py are empty. pyproject.toml identifies the package as POC package (beacon-only), uses setuptools.build_meta and lists a placeholder author.
limits: The DNS lookup resolves the local hostname; it neither encodes identity into a DNS label nor contacts the callback through DNS. There is no HTTP fallback branch.
The callback runs when setuptools invokes the registered install command, including compatible build/install flows. Importing the empty runtime module does not execute this callback.

PoC disclosure and the limited data favor a pentest explanation. Authorization and intended deployment are unknown; the distributed executable behavior is nonetheless a silent install-time identity export.
samples.verdict_reason: The package has no runtime product functionality and exports machine identity to a third-party collector as an installation side effect. On a machine without supplied authorized-test context, this is likely malicious.
samples.coverage: One distinct hostile behavior is supported: hostname/IP export. One hostile trait plus one suspicious callback trait is intentional; duplicating this one action to reach two hostile traits would misrepresent the evidence.

external_corroboration.note: Advisory corroborates host-info export and probable pentest packaging. Its general import-time claim is not true of the empty runtime module in these bytes.

samples.identity: VBScript launcher carrying a UTF-16LE Base64 PowerShell TCP command shell
behavior: WScript.Shell.Run launches powershell.exe with NoProfile, WindowStyle Hidden and EncodedCommand; Run window style is also 0, and False disables waiting for exit.
Decoded PowerShell connects a TCPClient to 192.0.2.42:4444, reads up to 65536 bytes, decodes received UTF-8 as commands and evaluates them with Invoke-Expression.
It combines stdout/stderr with Out-String, returns the resulting UTF-8 bytes over the same socket and continues until the connection closes. There is no authentication.
limits: The configured IP is a documentation-range address, suggesting a demonstration specimen rather than usable public infrastructure. Execution and concealment behavior are still concrete.
No operator authorization, legitimate remote-management product, or deployment provenance was supplied. No persistence is implemented.
samples.verdict_reason: The hidden, encoded launcher provides unauthenticated TCP command execution and replies, a reverse command-shell pattern. A possible test origin does not establish authorized deployment.
samples.coverage: Existing command-dispatch and hidden-window hostile findings retained; a neutral WSH Run matcher now recognizes quoted executable arguments.
